v.rationale: Both implementations use the same sound concurrency design. Each runs a transaction that locks the coupon row with lockForUpdate, checks for an existing redemption before the cap, and backs this up with a unique (coupon_id, user_id) index. Both return 201 or 200 based on wasRecentlyCreated and render a 409 with a message from a custom exception. Probes confirmed that both dispatch the event after commit and exactly once per new redemption, that a repeat call after other users have redeemed returns the same id with the current count, and that a coupon with zero capacity returns 409. The deciding difference is how a request without auth is handled. impl-1 changed bootstrap/app.php so that unauthenticated API requests do not redirect. That means a bearer client that sends no Accept header gets 401, and its tests cover this. impl-2 returns a 500 (Route [login] not defined) in that case, a real bug for the mobile clients the task describes. impl-2 has slightly better encapsulation: the event lives in the model, and the event class uses SerializesModels. It also has a real bearer-token test. But it relies on a clever setRawAttributes sync. impl-1 dispatches in the controller and adds unneeded retries. These are smaller points than impl-2's 500 error, so impl-1 ranks first.
